memo: CARETAKER EXEMPTION APPLIES. Member is a parent of two children ages 6 and 9. Per EX-CARETAKER, 'A parent, guardian, or caretaker relative of a dependent child age 13 or younger is exempt.' This exemption eliminates the 80-hour requirement entirely. Screening confirms: likely exemption caretaker_young_child. Per EX-OVERVIEW, 'If an exemption applies, the 80-hour requirement does not apply to you at all, and reporting hours is unnecessary.' STRATEGY: Submit birth certificate or benefits record showing both children's ages as proof. This is the strongest, fastest path. Member currently has pay stubs for 40h/month employment, but exemption claim makes hour counting unnecessary. Deadline is 2026-08-05 (18.6 days remaining). Member reports fear of losing coverage; this exemption eliminates that risk entirely if submitted with proper proof.
member_impact: Good news! You do NOT have to work 80 hours. Because you are taking care of two children ages 6 and 9, you are exempt from the work requirement. This exemption means the 80-hour rule does not apply to you at all. To claim your exemption, just send in a birth certificate or other record showing your children's ages (like a benefits letter or school enrollment). You have until August 5, 2026 to send it in. Once the state gets your proof, your coverage is safe and you do not have to report hours. You do not need to worry about being 40 hours short—your exemption covers you completely.
missing_documents: child birth certificate (for one or both children) OR benefits record showing child ages
recommended_actions: Gather the birth certificate for at least one of the two children (ages 6 and 9), OR obtain a benefits record, school enrollment letter, or similar document clearly showing their ages.
Attach the proof document(s) to your response to the state.
Include a short note: 'I am claiming the caretaker exemption. I am the parent of two children ages 6 and 9 (under age 13). Attached is proof of their ages.'
Keep a copy of everything you submit, with today's date written on it.

citations.quote: A parent, guardian, or caretaker relative of a dependent child age 13 or younger is exempt, as is a caretaker of a person with a disability. Proof is simple: the child's birth certificate, a benefits record showing the child's age, or documentation of the care relationship.
If an exemption applies, the 80-hour requirement does not apply to you at all, and reporting hours is unnecessary. Always check exemptions before counting hours.
Keep a copy, photo, or confirmation number for every document you submit and every report you make.
